summary: The client came back, and the reason for the silence was medical. After 12 days and 19 hours without a word — tying the longest client gap ever recorded on this account (Jul 30 → Aug 11) — Alex resurfaced on Aug 26 with 'Hey I’ve just had surgery so probably not for a few weeks unfortunately', paid the Aug 1–14 invoice in full to the changed account number, and posted the receipt. That kills last week's churn hypothesis: she did not move to the sales-team groupchat and she is not quietly exiting. She was recovering from an operation nobody at ALTR knew about, because in 12 days of silence not one person on this account asked her a single human question. Derrek's last message here is still Aug 13 — 15 days ago. Then ALTR did the worse thing: she told nine people she had just had surgery and nobody acknowledged it. Ronnie's reply, nine hours later, was 'Ok all good' followed by 'Will let the fans know and send the free content in mean time'. Stephski's only message of the week was 'Thank you!' — for the money. No 'are you okay', no 'what do you need', no adjustment of the plan. The second finding is commercial: she has just told the agency her content supply is stopping for weeks. Ronnie had sent a customs sheet on Aug 25 (the first content request on this account since Jul 6 — a 50-day pipeline gap of ALTR's own making), it landed the day after she went under, and there is no shoot-ahead plan, no vault audit and no revenue forecast for the recovery window. Everything else simply aged another seven days: @paigealexxo posting is 31 days past Michelle's 'posting will start this week' and 87 days past her first ask, the sales-team groupchat promised 'in the next few hours' on Aug 12 is 16 days unconfirmed, Derrek's 'plenty of updates starting next week' is 27 days old with zero updates delivered, and the money ALTR owes her still has no written balance 17 days after 'Sending'. Payment itself was 4 days past the requested window and, as ever, nobody had to fight her for it.

health.rationale: Up 11 points from 41. The single largest risk on this account last week — that a client who had gone dark on 3 of 21 days was quietly churning — is now disproven: she returned on Aug 26, explained the silence (surgery), paid the Aug 1–14 invoice in full and posted the receipt, and did so to the changed account number, so the fourth-banking-change risk also failed to materialize. That is worth double digits. It is not worth more, because the week exposed something worse than a payment risk: ALTR let a client go 12 days without a single human check-in, learned she had been in surgery, and responded with 'Ok all good' and 'Thank you!'. Derrek has not written in this chat for 15 days. Nothing was delivered against six standing promises (IG posting 31 days, groupchat invite 16, proactive updates 27, ALTR's debt to her 17, link-preview image 33, OF revenue plan 61), the invoice was paid 4 days late with no chase, and her content supply is now blocked 'for a few weeks' with no plan on file. Score capped in the low 50s: the relationship survived on her goodwill, not on ALTR's service.
